sections.label: Overview
sections.purpose: Concise scholarly summary of the figure, name, tradition, and significance.
sections.body:
**Illapa** ​(*illapa*) ‌— ‌Thunder, Lightning, ​War ​· ​Thunder ​— ​belongs to ‌the ​Incan ​tradition, ‌where ​it is ‌catalogued ​under ‌the ​domain ​"Thunder, Lightning, ​War". ​The ​name ‌means ​"Thunder".

**Illapa** ‌is ​thunder, ‌lightning, ​war. ‌The name ​means ‌"Thunder" ​and ​belongs ‌to ‌the incan ‌tradition.

​PuniCodex ​restores ‌the ​name as ​**Illapa** ‌and ​serves ​its ‌temple at ​[its ‌temple](https://punicodex.com/illapa/). ​The ​restoration ​needs no ​distinctive ‌letters ‌or ​diacritics ‌its ASCII ​form ​would ‌lose, ‌which ‌places ‌the name ​in ‌Tier ​2. ​The ​plain ASCII ‌form ​*illapa* ​survives ​as ‌a modern ​convenience ​imposed ​by ‌the ​early domain-name ‌system; ​the ‌restoration, ​not ‌the fallback, ‌is ​the ​form ​the ​project defends ‌as ‌philologically ​complete.

sections.label: The Name
sections.purpose: Etymology, ASCII constraint, Unicode restoration, name variations, tier classification.
sections.body:
No ​indigenous written ‌attestation ‌survives ​for this ​name; ​**Illapa** is ​a ​scholarly transliteration ‌of ​the ​reconstructed spoken ‌form. ​Etymologically the ‌name ​means "Thunder".

‌The ​ASCII ​form *illapa* ​survives ​only because ​the ‌early ​domain-name system ‌could ​not carry ‌diacritics; ​it is ‌a ​technological ‌compromise, not ​an ​ancient spelling. ‌The ‌Unicode restoration ‌**Illapa** ​recovers ​the full ‌diacritic ​detail of ​the ‌scholarly ​transliteration directly ​in ‌the address ​bar. ‌The restoration ​needs ​no ​distinctive letters ​or ‌diacritics its ‌ASCII ​form ‌would lose, ​which ​places the ‌name ‌in Tier ‌2.

‌The ​letter-by-letter transformation ‌runs:

​- **i** ​→ ​**I** — ‌Same, ​capitalized
​- **l** ​→ ‌**l** — ​Same
​- ​**l** → ‌**l** ​— Same
‌- ​**a** → ‌**a** ​— ‌Same
- ‌**p** ​→ **p** ​— ​Same
- ​**a** ‌→ ‌**a** — ​Same

sections.purpose: IPA reconstruction, phoneme breakdown, approximation, kin forms.
sections.body:
The ​reconstructed ‌pronunciation of ‌the ​name ​is ​**/illapa/** — ​Restored ​scholarly ‌form.

​Phoneme by ​phoneme:

‌- ​**illapa** ‌— ​The canonical ‌restored ​form ​Illapa.

​For the ​modern ​speaker, ‌the ​closest approximation ‌is: ​Say ‌"illapa" ​with the ‌stress ​and ‌length ​implied by ​the ‌scholarly ‌restoration ‌"Illapa".

​The ASCII ​form ‌"illapa" ​is ​a DNS ‌compromise; ​the ​restoration ‌"Illapa" preserves ​the ‌name's ​scholarly ​dignity.

The ​pronunciation ​given ‌above ‌reconstructs the ​sound ‌world ​in ​which ‌Illapa was ‌invoked. ‌Modern ‌speakers ​should not ‌expect ​exact ​identity ​with ancient ‌phonology; ​the ​reconstruction ​is a ‌scholarly ​compass, ​not ​a performance ‌prescription. ​The ‌restoration ​Illapa ‌keeps the ​prosodic ‌information ‌visible ​even when ​the ​name ​is ‌typed in ‌plain ​ASCII.

sections.label: Mythology
sections.purpose: Core myths, primary narratives, and textual evidence.
sections.body:
The ​stories of ‌Illapa ‌place ​thunder, lightning, ​war ​at ​the center ​of ‌a living ​mythological ​world.

‌### Origins ​(Myth)

‌Illapa ​appears in ‌incan ​tradition as ​thunder, ​lightning, ​war. The ​name's ‌meaning, ​"Thunder", shapes ‌the ​narratives told ‌about ​this ‌figure.

### ​Worship ‌and ​Memory (Cult)

​Devotees ‌and later ‌tradition-keepers ‌preserved ​Illapa in ​ritual, ‌text, ​and iconography, ​ensuring ‌the name ​survived ​into ‌the modern ​scholarly ‌record.

​The myths ​of ​Illapa survive ​in ‌fragments, ‌summaries, and ​later ‌retellings. ​Each version ​reflects ‌the interests ‌of ‌its ‌tellers — ​poets, ‌priests, ​philosophers, and ​scholars. ​The PuniCodex ‌entry ​does ​not privilege ​a ‌single ​version; it ​gathers ​the attestations ‌so ​that ‌readers can ​compare ‌them. ​The restoration ‌Illapa ‌gives the ​figure ​a ​stable name ​around ‌which ‌these variants ​orbit.

sections.purpose: Sites, inscriptions, artifacts, and physical attestations.
sections.body:
No ​monument, ‌inscription, ‌or ​artifact in ​the ​current ​PuniCodex ​corpus ‌is ​yet ​assigned to ‌Illapa ​with ‌certainty. ​That ‌absence ​should ​be read ​honestly: ​for ​a ‌Incan ​name ‌of ​this ‌type the ​material ‌record ​is ‌expected ​to ​be ‌thin, and ‌the ‌primary ​evidence ​remains ‌the ​textual ​testimony gathered ‌in ​the ​Scholarly ‌Sources ​section.

‌Were ​such ​evidence to ​surface, ​it ‌would ‌take ​recognizable ‌forms: ​votive or ​dedicatory ‌inscriptions ‌naming ‌Illapa, ‌sanctuary ​or ‌cult remains ​tied ​to ​thunder ‌and ​iconography ​matching ​its ‌traditional attributes ​(name ​and ​domain). ‌Each ​candidate ‌would ​be weighed ‌against ​the ‌reconstructed ‌form ​of ​the ​name before ​entering ‌the ‌scholarly ​record.

sections.label: Meditation & Reflection
sections.purpose: Contemplative or interpretive essay on the figure's enduring meaning.
sections.body:
To ​contemplate ‌Illapa ‌is to ​hold ​the ​idea ​of ​thunder, Lightning, ‌War ​in ​the ‌mind ​and to ‌ask ​what ‌of ​it ​endures. The ​name ​means ​"Thunder" ‌— ​and a ‌name ​that ‌carries ​its ‌meaning so ​openly ‌invites ​meditation ​rather ‌than ‌mere recollection. ‌The ​tradition ​remembers ‌the ​name as ​thunder, ‌Lightning, ​War ​· ‌Thunder.

Sit ​with ‌the ​restored ​form ​— Illapa ​— ‌and ‌the ​diacritics ‌themselves become ​the ​practice: ‌each ‌mark ‌is ‌a small ​act ‌of ​attention, ​a ​refusal to ‌let ​the ​plain ​ASCII ‌form *illapa* ​stand ​in ​for ‌the ​whole. What ‌the ​tradition ‌preserved ​in ‌this name, ‌the ​restoration ​asks ​the ​reader to ‌preserve ‌in ​turn.
